amr_method.evidence_quote: All strains were tested for ceftazidime (CAZ), cefoxitin (FOX), imipenem (IMI), and meropenem (MEM) MICs by microdilution systems, while CZA MICs were tested using the CZA gradient test (Liofilchem, Roseto degli Abruzzi, Italy).

study_setting.evidence_quote: a total of 10,731 consecutive, nonduplicate enterobacterial isolates were collected from patients' specimens in a 252-bed oncology hospital in Sofia, Bulgaria. Clinical specimens originated from infected or colonized patients admitted to hospital wards or attending outpatient departments.

amr_study.evidence_quote: Among the 10,731 isolates, tested for high-level resistance to aminoglycosides, 150 (1.4%) showed concomitant resistance to gentamicin and amikacin with no zone of inhibition around the discs and MICs > 256 mg/L. No isolate was found with high-level resistance to apramycin. PCR analysis revealed the presence of 16S rRNA methyltransferase genes in all 150 isolates.

amr_target.evidence_quote: All isolates were screened for high-level resistance to amikacin, gentamicin and apramycin by the Kirby–Bauer disc diffusion method. Isolates that exhibited no zone of inhibition around 15 µg apramycin discs or 30 µg amikacin and 10 µg gentamicin discs were further confirmed by gradient strip MIC

amr_method.evidence_quote: All isolates were screened for high-level resistance to amikacin, gentamicin and apramycin by the Kirby–Bauer disc diffusion method... When they showed an MIC > 256 mg/L to amikacin and gentamicin, indicating N7-G1405 methyltransferase production, or MIC > 256 mg/L to apramycin, indicating the N1-A1408 enzyme, a multiplex PCR to detect armA, rmtA-F and npmA was performed

study_setting.evidence_quote: Organisms added to the AR Isolate Bank are obtained mostly from CDC surveillance programs, outbreak investigations, and isolates sent to the CDC for reference testing. The CDC has also reached out to domestic and international partners to obtain isolates with new or unusual resistance that are not part of the existing CDC collection. In addition, pharmaceutical companies have provided bacterial isolates from their collections for deposit into the AR Isolate Bank.

amr_study.evidence_quote: a curated repository of bacterial isolates with an assortment of clinically important resistance mechanisms that have been phenotypically and genotypically characterized

amr_target.evidence_quote: The first panel added was the Enterobacteriaceae carbapenem breakpoint panel (31 isolates)... The second panel was the Gram-negative carbapenemase detection panel (80 isolates)... The third panel was the Enterobacteriaceae carbapenemase diversity panel (53 isolates)... The ceftolozane-tazobactam panel (30 isolates) and ceftazidime-avibactam panel (30 isolates) were developed in collaboration with pharmaceutical companies.

amr_method.evidence_quote: Reference broth microdilution is performed to obtain antibiotic susceptibility testing (AST) data in accordance with CLSI standards. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) is also performed to achieve better understanding of the genetic basis of resistance in each isolate.

coverage_basis: The paper describes the entire AR Isolate Bank (496 isolates across 14 panels spanning many bacterial genera and species as of June 2017) but does not state how many Klebsiella isolates are included. The 13 Klebsiella samples in PRJNA497260 are an unspecified subset. Pattern B applies: the article's sequenced count (496 across all taxa) is far larger than E=13, indicating this accession covers only a small slice of the full bank.

country.evidence_quote: The CDC has also reached out to domestic and international partners to obtain isolates with new or unusual resistance that are not part of the existing CDC collection. We will continue to develop and maintain international partnerships to obtain isolates with resistance mechanisms that have not yet been detected in the United States.

notes: SIZING (Pattern B): E_taxon=13 Klebsiella, E_total=13; the paper describes 496 isolates across 14 panels and many species — this accession covers only a small, taxonomically-selected portion of the full bank. AMR_METHOD is not_gradeable: the paper describes both phenotypic AST (broth microdilution) and molecular/genotypic characterisation (WGS, PCR-based carbapenemase detection) without specifying which drove selection for the 13 Klebsiella samples. STUDY_SETTING is not_gradeable: sources span CDC surveillance programs, outbreak investigations, reference-testing referrals, international partners, and pharmaceutical collections — insufficient evidence to fix a single setting for all 13 Klebsiella records. COHORT_AGE, HOST, ISOLATION_SOURCE, COLLECTION_DATE, and COUNTRY are all not backfillable due to the heterogeneous multi-panel, multi-species nature of the bank and absence of specimen-level detail in the paper.

ENA reports ena_taxon_samples=10 (Klebsiella) = ena_total_samples=10, which almost certainly reflects taxonomic misclassification of E. coli as Klebsiella (or a broader Enterobacteriaceae node) in the ENA taxonomy database rather than genuine Klebsiella isolates.
